name: Polymarket versus Kalshi BTC window dislocation
description: Cross-venue comparison of the market-implied up probability for two BTC up/down contracts whose settlement windows close at the same instant. The instance is multi-market scoped with exactly two legs, kalshi then polymarket in sorted order, and binds only when the two bound market generations satisfy the alignment rule: window_close is byte-identical after RFC 3339 normalization to UTC (exact_close), the two windows overlap, and both markets are open. Any other relation publishes non-ready with window_alignment_mismatch and no instance is bound. implied_up_<venue> is that venue's affirmative_midpoint from btc.<venue>.prediction_quote and the bid/ask legs are its affirmative_bid and affirmative_ask. dislocation is implied_up_polymarket minus implied_up_kalshi in probability units and dislocation_bps is that times ten thousand. The two contracts settle on different benchmarks (Chainlink BTC/USD 60-second TWAP versus the CF Benchmarks BRTI sixty-print average) at different strikes, so the raw difference is not an arbitrage: strike_difference_absolute is polymarket strike minus kalshi strike and strike_difference_bps divides it by the kalshi strike times ten thousand. model_adjustment is the strike difference expressed in probability by the in-stack model, phi_cdf of the polymarket standardized moneyness minus phi_cdf of the kalshi standardized moneyness, taken verbatim as the published probability fields of btc.polymarket.fair_up_probability@1.0.0 and btc.kalshi.fair_up_probability@1.0.0; this identity does no modelling of its own. strike_adjusted_dislocation is dislocation minus model_adjustment. state is dislocated when the absolute strike_adjusted_dislocation exceeds dislocation_threshold and aligned otherwise; dislocation_threshold defaults to 0.02. direction names which venue is rich on the adjusted reading. underlying_mismatch is true whenever the two rules cards declare different settlement_benchmark values and tie_rule_mismatch is true whenever comparator or tie_outcome differ; both are published on every update because they are the standing caveat on the reading, and on the currently listed contracts underlying_mismatch is true and tie_rule_mismatch is false. Ready output requires both legs bound, both quotes uncrossed and no more than 10000 milliseconds old, both fair probability inputs ready, and time_to_close_ms strictly positive. Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
